questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always wanted to go to Australia, and it seemed like the perfect opportunity to study there.

questions.answer: It was very easy. Monash University made everything very smooth and easy.

questions.answer: The introduction and orientation week for the exchange students was a good assistance for settling in.

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was VERY satisfied. Would recommend that everybody who goes to Melbourne stay at Beach House in St Kilda. I shared a studio apartment with my boyfriend and met other students who shared a 3 room apartment in the building. You had access to pool, spa, gym, cinema, bowling, sky bar, and it was very social and close to the beach. The price wasn't too high when I was there.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be a good idea to look in Facebook housing groups or AirBnb. It can be a bit challenging to find affordable and good accommodation.

Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: In the orientation week they had an open workshop where there are multiple people there to help you registering for the courses you are interested in. The website you use for registration is also very simple.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Tutors and guides helped you.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful and got into the courses I wanted with no problem.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would advice you to go to the orientation week.

questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was good. I found it easier to get high grades in Australia than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had way more online teaching than I have at UCPH. All my lectures were online, so I only had to be at the university physically when I had tutorials.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:
Organisational Behaviour

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the course "Men, masculinity and society" if you are interested in learning about masculinity/different forms of masculinity, the gender hierarchy, and much more.

questions.answer: There were countless clubs available for students to join. Gym, salsa, netball

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the gym, they have sauna too.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: In the weekends I would recommend going on trips. It is very easy to drive to The Great Ocean Road and Phillip Island from Melbourne.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, it felt very European.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It is a good idea to learn some Australian slang words since they use slang a lot.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nature and the people. The nature is incredibly beautiful and the people are very sociable and kind.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
I would tell you to find accommodation in Melbourne city since the campus is a bit far away. Since a lot of the teaching was online, it was more fun to stay close to the city because you didn't go to campus every day. It is easy to go with public transportation to Caulfield and Clayton campus from the city, it just takes a bit more time, but it is worth it to stay in the city. 
I would also tell you to socialize with the other exchange students, I met so many great people. 
And get the app where you can see the campus if you are going to the Clayton campus, since it is huge. Be there in good time before class.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a free shuttlebus between the Clayton and the Caulfield campus, so it is easy to have classes at both campuses. The ride is about 20 minutes.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I found it a bit difficult to write the first research paper in English, also because they write a bit differently from what I am used to. But it worked out fine.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
